classes.name: Normal
classes.prompt_summary: Healthy bearing: operating conditions may change amplitude and spectral scale, but there is no persistent bearing-fault-order impact train, modulation pattern, or localized resonance burst.

descriptions.text: The rolling bearing is healthy and has no localized defect on either race or the rolling elements.
Rolling contact remains mechanically continuous, so no damaged surface repeatedly interrupts the load path.
The vibration lacks a persistent train of impulsive events, fault-order harmonics, characteristic sidebands, and short resonance bursts attributable to bearing damage.

Speed, load, sensor position, and bearing family may change overall amplitude and frequency scale, but a healthy state does not develop a repeatable localized-fault pattern tied to bearing kinematics.
Isolated broadband fluctuations or operating-condition transients alone are insufficient evidence of inner-race, outer-race, or rolling-element damage.

symptoms.name: Stable vibration
symptoms.description: The vibration amplitude remains stable without a repeating train of localized impacts.

symptoms.name: No fault-frequency peak
symptoms.description: No persistent peak or harmonic pattern is associated with a bearing characteristic fault frequency.

symptoms.name: Low impulsiveness
symptoms.description: The signal has low impulsiveness and lacks high-frequency resonance bursts caused by localized damage.

classes.name: InnerRace
classes.prompt_summary: Inner-race fault: a rotating race defect repeatedly crosses the load zone, producing BPFI-related impacts, shaft-speed modulation or sidebands, and localized resonance bursts whose absolute frequencies move with operating speed.

descriptions.text: The bearing has a localized defect on the inner race, which rotates with the shaft relative to the load zone.
Each rolling element crossing the inner-race defect produces an impact whose amplitude changes as the defect moves through the loaded region.
Evidence includes components near the ball-pass frequency of the inner race, its harmonics, shaft-frequency sidebands or modulation, and impact-excited resonance bursts.
When speed or bearing geometry changes, the absolute BPFI frequency changes, while the kinematic order relationship and rotating-load-zone modulation remain the stable diagnostic concept.

Compared with a stationary outer-race defect, an inner-race defect more often exhibits shaft-related amplitude modulation and sidebands; compared with rolling-element damage, its impact intervals are more strongly tied to BPFI.

symptoms.name: BPFI impact train
symptoms.description: Repeated impacts occur near the ball-pass frequency of the inner race and its harmonics.

symptoms.name: Rotational sidebands
symptoms.description: Inner-race fault components exhibit sidebands or amplitude modulation related to shaft rotation.

symptoms.name: Resonance bursts
symptoms.description: Localized inner-race impacts excite short high-frequency resonance bursts in the vibration signal.

classes.name: Ball
classes.prompt_summary: Rolling-element fault: damage on a ball or roller produces BSF-related and often less stationary impacts, with load-zone modulation, cage or shaft sidebands, and resonance bursts that vary as the damaged element changes orientation.

descriptions.text: The bearing has localized damage on a rolling element rather than on the inner or outer race.
The damaged rolling element alternately contacts the races and changes orientation while entering and leaving the load zone, producing variable impacts.
Evidence includes ball-spin-frequency components, harmonics, cage- or shaft-related sidebands, irregular impact spacing, and load-zone-dependent resonance bursts.
Speed, load, and bearing geometry shift the absolute BSF components and impact strength, but the rolling-element modulation mechanism remains the stable semantic cue.
Rolling-element faults are usually less stationary than a fixed outer-race impact train and are not dominated by the BPFI pattern and shaft modulation expected for an inner-race defect.

symptoms.name: Ball-spin components
symptoms.description: Spectral components and harmonics occur near the ball spin frequency.

symptoms.name: Load-zone modulation
symptoms.description: Impact amplitude changes as the damaged rolling element enters and leaves the bearing load zone.

symptoms.name: Irregular rolling-element impacts
symptoms.description: Rolling-element damage produces less stationary impact intervals with cage- or shaft-related sidebands.

classes.name: OuterRace
classes.prompt_summary: Outer-race fault: rolling elements repeatedly pass a stationary race defect, producing BPFO-related periodic impacts and resonance bursts with comparatively stable amplitude when the defect remains in the loaded region.

descriptions.text: The bearing has a localized defect on the stationary outer race.
Rolling elements repeatedly pass the fixed outer-race defect, generating a periodic impact at a spatially stationary location.
Evidence includes the ball-pass frequency of the outer race, its harmonics, a comparatively stationary impact train, and periodic high-frequency resonance bursts.
Speed and bearing geometry shift the absolute BPFO frequency, while the fixed-defect mechanism and the corresponding kinematic order remain stable diagnostic information.
Unlike an inner-race fault, a loaded outer-race defect usually has weaker shaft-periodic amplitude modulation; unlike rolling-element damage, its impact sequence is more stationary and BPFO-related.

symptoms.name: BPFO impact train
symptoms.description: Repeated impacts occur near the ball-pass frequency of the outer race and its harmonics.

symptoms.name: Stationary impact amplitude
symptoms.description: A stationary outer-race defect produces a comparatively stable periodic impact amplitude.

symptoms.name: Outer-race resonance bursts
symptoms.description: Periodic outer-race impacts excite high-frequency structural resonance bursts.
